targets.html:
03 / THE BENCH

From a command
to a check.

Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation. My fixture makes its response available to bench instruments.

Ada wrote the firmware and scheduled its power states. State tables and timing diagrams are part of her working documents; this is not a reproduction of that firmware.

I wrote the firmware and built the fixture. A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end.

Command → board → fixture → observation.
An explanatory relationship, not electrical wiring.

FROM THE SUPPLIED NOTES

The source behind
the story.

“Battery spreadsheet uses measured sleep and transmit current with an assumed reporting interval.”

From the fictional Mosslink lab notes. The spreadsheet, current values and reporting interval are not supplied.

Back to the question ↑

The longest run was 72 hours. Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle.

Forty engineering samples were assembled. Six were tested on the bench. None went to customers.

One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.

Ada wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture. A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end.

Ada and Mosslink are fictional. Illustrative bench model: shapes and connections are explanatory, not a photograph, circuit diagram, wiring plan or measured signal.
